Theorem
[Geometric structure of the thin part] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0210 1. ch31:31.43\group Margulis lemma

For $n\ge 3$ and $\varepsilon \le \varepsilon _n$, the thin part is a disjoint union of cusp ends, Margulis tubes around short geodesics, and (at exceptional lengths) geodesic circles. Cusp pieces have metric $dr^2+e^{-2r}g_{\rm flat}$, while tubes are modeled on $\sum _i(x^i ds+dx^i)^2+ds^2$.
